content:
AIChatApp Architecture Reference

- AIChatApp.API is the backend for authentication, JWT issuance, 2FA endpoints, chat orchestration, chat history persistence, response reporting, backoffice APIs, ML.NET reviewer workflow endpoints, and local LLM access.
- AIChatApp.Gateway is the reverse proxy entry point. It applies API key checks, rate limiting, and path forwarding to the API.
- AIChatApp.Core contains shared entities, DbContexts, middleware, configuration helpers, assistant profile data, prompt/knowledge models, and path utilities used across projects.
- AIChatApp.Web is the Blazor frontend for login, 2FA management, chat, backoffice, FAQs, Backoffice Machine Learning modals, copy/read/continue/report actions, and streaming chat.
- AIChatApp.MLTraining contains the ML.NET reviewer models, training service, runtime reviewer service, and workflow service.
- Reviewer training data, jobs, and model registry views are managed from Backoffice > Machine Learning.
- AIChatApp.Console is a local console client for direct testing.

Web workspace routes:
- /chat - main documentation chat assistant.
- /backoffice - admin validation workspace for reports, prompts, knowledge, users, and reviewer controls.
- Backoffice > Machine Learning - reviewer training data, training jobs, and model registry modals using the same admin session.
- /faqs - readable FAQ page loaded from documentation knowledge.

Gateway routing overview:
- /auth/* -> /api/auth/*
- /chat/* -> /api/chat/*
- /chathistory/* -> /api/chathistory/*

Chat behavior overview:
- ask-stream is the SSE endpoint for streaming responses.
- ask-ai is the JSON endpoint for non-streaming responses.
- ask-continue is the JSON endpoint for finishing a cut response.

UI behavior overview:
- Chat has collapsible conversations, workspace, and account sidebar sections.
- Backoffice groups sidebar navigation into Workspaces, Validation, Machine Learning, and Administration.
- FAQs has a workspace sidebar and a scrollable FAQ content area.
- Workspace navigation uses one theme color per app area instead of separate colors per link.
